001.summary: Game one of four at Alex's, three-player. The pilot mulliganed into a hand he calls "structurally dead": a clean land base, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist, and zero goblins — the whole storm-and-copy half in hand with nothing to multiply through. He files it as a bad draw and a bad keep rather than a deck problem and made no changes; the entry's decklist_sha256 matches the current list, so the 99 is unchanged since.

cards.why: in the opening hand and inert: the note says he "had the entire storm-and-copy half of the engine in hand and nothing to multiply through".
same hand, same reason — a copy engine "with no body to target is a hand that does nothing, however good the individual cards look".

decisions.spot: the game-one mulligan: a clean land base, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist, and zero goblins — keep or ship

takeaways: The mulligan gate for this deck is GOBLIN PRESENCE, not cantrip density — the pilot's own words.
A hand of cantrips plus a copy engine with no body to target does nothing however good the individual cards look; the pilot's verdict is that he should have shipped it.
No deck change follows from this game: the pilot reads it as a bad draw and a bad keep, and the list stays pinned at v1.0.0, precon as printed.

open_questions.question: After mulligans, how often does this 99 present an opening hand with at least one cheap goblin body — the gate the pilot says he should be mulliganing to?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot has named goblin presence as his keep criterion but has no figure for how often the deck can meet it, so he cannot know whether the gate is a reasonable one to hold or one that would ship too many hands.

002.summary: Game one of three at Oliver's, five-player. The pilot kept three basics, a utility land and Krenko, Mob Boss — "land and a value engine and NO SMALL GOBLINS" — and with the instants and sorceries all expensive the cantrip half never turned over and the engine never assembled. The table was three mono-red decks and Oliver killed it on turn five off Krenko tokens and pings. This is the second logged game lost to the same keep criterion.

opponents.evidence: Tom on Purphoros doing the same
five-player pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan
five-player pod: Sean, Oliver, Tom, Alex, Ryan

cards.why: kept as the hand's value engine; the note says the hand had "land and a value engine and NO SMALL GOBLINS", and "the engine never assembled".

decisions.spot: the opener at Oliver's: three basics, a utility land and Krenko, Mob Boss, with no cheap goblins — keep or mulligan (the same decision as entry 001, on a different hand)

takeaways: The pilot restates the same gate he named in entry 001: GOBLIN PRESENCE gates the mulligan, not cantrip density, and cheap goblin bodies are non-negotiable for the deck to function.
In this game the instants and sorceries in hand were all expensive, so the cantrip half never turned over — the fuel stage failed alongside the body pile, not instead of it.
The pod itself was a factor the pilot names: three mono-red decks, and the red density took the game over before his own engine came online.

open_questions.question: Does the 99 carry enough cheap goblin bodies, and cheap enough instants and sorceries, to support the keep criterion the pilot has now stated twice — or is the gate unmeetable as the list is built?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both logged games are losses with the same shape: a hand the pilot liked, no small goblins, engine never assembled. Two games is thin, but it is the same failure twice and the pilot has twice declined to change the deck over it, so the doctor should say whether the keep rule or the list is the thing that has to move.
